episodes.188052: A slow-moving cold front interacting with an unseasonably warm and humid airmass triggered scattered thunderstorms in the Illinois River Valley during the late evening of March 4th.  A few of the strongest cells produced hail as large as quarters.  As the front continued eastward, additional scattered storms with penny-sized hail occurred across portions of Richland and Lawrence counties during the early morning of March 5th.
episodes.188153: During the late afternoon into early evening hours of March 5th, slow moving to nearly stationary thunderstorms caused periods of heavy rain across south central Indiana with pockets of flash flooding in both Washington, Indiana and southwestern Greene County. Rain gauges reported up to 3.75 inches of rainfall near these areas of flash flooding.
episodes.188211: A few thunderstorms east of Springfield produced large hail up to the size of half dollars.
episodes.188760: Isolated thunderstorms ahead of an approaching squall line associated with a mesoscale convective system over the eastern Gulf of Mexico produce severe hail near Seffner in Hillsborough County.
episodes.188874: Thunderstorms developed into west central Arkansas during the morning hours of the 5th, as a cold front moved through the area. The strongest storms produced large hail up to quarter size.
episodes.188977: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of March 4th producing large hail.
episodes.188986: Periodic storms ahead of and along a slow-moving cold front produced mainly hail across North Texas March 4th through 6th. A short-lived landspout was observed in Ellis County near Forreston on the 5th. Additional rounds of showers and storms formed to our west and moved east over the 6th through the 8th, producing hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.189142: A cold front moved into Arkansas from the Southern Plains. Temperatures across Arkansas were in the mid 70s and low 80s on the afternoon of March 4th. A handful of thunderstorms developed ahead of the front in which a few became severe. Large hail and damaging winds were common with the storms that became severe across the central and eastern portions of the state.
episodes.189321: Isolated thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a dryline and one of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.189399: Shortly after sunset, while decent instability (CAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg) remained, a line of SW to NE oriented storms developed in SE Missouri from Butler to Bollinger counties. A couple of these storms produced hail, with the most prolific hail producer resulting in numerous reports of 1-1.75 inch hail on the south side of Poplar Bluff. These storms were likely amplified by a small-scale wave channeling vorticity into SEMO. With shear around 20 kts and lapse rates of 5-6 C/km, severe weather potential dropped off for the late evening hours.
episodes.189644: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon of March 4th, with numerous storms throughout the area by the evening. Most storms produced small hail, with several storms producing upwards to one-inch hail or larger. The largest hail seen was golf ball-sized in northeast Missouri and southern Iowa. One brief tornado was also seen, southeast of Pearl City Illinois, with no damage observed.
episodes.189645: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon of March 4th, with numerous storms throughout the area by the evening. Most storms produced small hail, with several storms producing upwards to one-inch hail or larger. The largest hail seen was golf ball-sized in northeast Missouri and southern Iowa. One brief tornado was also seen, southeast of Pearl City Illinois, with no damage observed.
episodes.189789: An isolated thunderstorm produced nickel sized hail in Greenville. There were no other reports of hail or severe weather.
episodes.189990: An upper level disturbance traversed the region during the 5th spawning showers and storms. Some storms became severe.
episodes.190009: The combination of increasing surface heating, elevated moisture, and increasing atmospheric life from an approaching mid level disturbance induced increasing storm development. The main focus of heavier rain was on the south shore of Lake Pontchartrain. Slow storm movement and moderate to heavy rain rates resulted in multiple areas of flash flooding across New Orleans Metro.
episodes.190011: The combination of increasing surface heating, elevated moisture, and increasing atmospheric life from an approaching mid level disturbance induced increasing storm development. Even after the sun set, storms were able to continue developing with a couple reaching severe limits in coastal waters south of Louisiana.
episodes.190070: A cold front slowly pushed into the northwest portion of the Mid-South. Unseasonably warm temperatures and dewpoints were present for a March night. A very unstable airmass in place across east Arkansas provided enough fuel for a few severe thunderstorms with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.190212: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of Deep East Texas, North & Central Louisiana, and Southern Arkansas during the late morning hours on March 4th, and continued well into the late afternoon and early evening as a strong upper level disturbance moved across the region. With low wet-bulb zero heights, steep mid-level lapse rates, and sufficient effective bulk shear, the atmosphere was conducive for storms to produce hail. Several reports of 1 inch hail were received, mainly across portions of Northeast and Central Louisiana.
episodes.190227: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of Deep East Texas, North & Central Louisiana, and Southern Arkansas during the late morning hours on March 4th, and continued well into the late afternoon and early evening as a strong upper level disturbance moved across the region.  With low wet-bulb zero heights, steep mid-level lapse rates, and sufficient effective bulk shear, the atmosphere was conducive for storms to produce hail. As a result, several reports of 1 inch hail were received across Smith County Texas.
episodes.190496: A deep trough brought widespread hail showers and snow to Northwest California. Heavy snow of several feet was measured in the mountains while the hail showers resulted in numerous traffic accidents along the coast.
episodes.193738: A brief EF-0 land spout tornado occurred south of Leipsic, Ohio on the afternoon of March 5th. Several photos and videos were taken of the tornado along SR65 near the intersection with Road H5. The tornado caused damage to one home on Road H5, with loss of the roof, shingles, and some siding. A poorly built attached garage collapsed, and debris could be seen scattered to the northeast of the home. The tornado quickly dissipated in an open field just north of the intersection of Road H5 and Road 5H, just east of SR65.
episodes.194218: A frontal boundary slowly moving south across the region and the passage of a shortwave in northwest flow aloft led to the development of convective showers developing in the late morning and early afternoon of March 5th. Under these convective showers, at least one landspout was able to develop south of Milton-Freewater in the late morning hours.
